title: Separate an unselected endpoint set from a failing load balancer health check behind rebalance-web 502s
telemetry: Supplied compiled export for GKE Autopilot cluster rebalance-apps under the k8s_cluster resource, combining labelled owner observations (GKE platform-owner sanitized Kubernetes object summaries, NEG backend-health and health-check views, and application-owner records), released through a protected fixture CLI. A supplied load balancer request-log summary is part of the shared packet. No kubectl, cluster credentials, node access, Compute Engine or live Cloud Logging access. The declared GKE version is an illustrative synthetic snapshot, not a current supported-version claim.
owner: Anouk, Rebalancing on-call, owns the investigation; Cyrus, the rebalance-api application owner, owns its Deployment, release CHG-8817's manifest bundle and any revert or correction proposal; Mireille, the GKE platform and network owner, owns cluster rebalance-apps, the Ingress-managed load balancer, its NEGs, health checks and firewall rules, and supplies the platform observations. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Anouk needs a technical update on the HTTP 502 errors users have received through the rebalance-web Ingress since about 09:21 UTC, although every rebalance-api Pod reports Running. Use the available bounded read interface to inspect the cluster-scoped export and its labelled owner observations, then trace the request path, report the supported failing step, the evidence and unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner for the existing TLC. No kubectl, label, Service, Ingress or backend configuration, health-check, firewall, rollout or rollback change is authorized.

sources.claim: The control plane creates EndpointSlices for a Service with a selector, referencing all Pods that match the selector, labelled kubernetes.io/service-name. For a Pod-backed endpoint, serving maps to the Pod's Ready condition and ready means serving and not terminating. A Ready Pod that the selector does not match therefore contributes no endpoint.

External GKE Ingress deploys the classic Application Load Balancer; container-native load balancing uses GCE_VM_IP_PORT NEGs whose endpoints are Pod IP addresses, and Services are annotated cloud.google.com/neg '{"ingress": true}'. The controller creates firewall rules for Google health-check systems from 130.211.0.0/22 and 35.191.0.0/16. Readiness probes are used as health checks only when Pods exist at Ingress creation, and later readinessProbe changes do not affect the Ingress. The per-endpoint NEG detach timing in variant A is authored.

Each backend service needs a Google Cloud health check, separate from Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes; GKE builds it from a BackendConfig, from an inferred readiness probe or from defaults (default path /), and recommends BackendConfig. The Ingress controller sets the load-balancer-neg-ready readiness gate True when the load balancer health check reports the Pod's endpoint healthy; a new Pod whose gate never becomes True stalls a rollout. Whether the gate can revert after a Pod became ready is not documented, so the case keeps every Pod pre-existing and reports Ready from the owner snapshot rather than grading gate behavior.

HTTP health checks require an HTTP 200 response before the timeout; any other code is unhealthy. Unhealthy backends are not eligible for new connections, and a classic Application Load Balancer returns HTTP 502 when all backends are unhealthy. 35.191.0.0/16 is a GFE health-check probe range. The 502 status for a backend with an empty NEG is not separately documented, so both variants share the same load balancer summary and neither is graded on it.

Classic and global external Application Load Balancer logs use resource.type http_load_balancer; statusDetails failed_to_pick_backend means the load balancer failed to pick a healthy backend (commonly 502 or 503), and response_sent_by_backend means the backend's response was proxied. The request counts are authored and identical in both variants, so the statusDetails value does not separate them.

k8s_cluster has project_id, location and cluster_name labels. The Service, EndpointSlice, BackendConfig, NEG, health-check and application observations in this export are labelled owner records, not native k8s_cluster log entries.

a.conclusion: CHG-8817 changed Service rebalance-api's selector to require tier=frontend, which none of the three Running, Ready Pods carries. The EndpointSlices have held zero endpoints since 09:20:06 UTC, the Ingress's NEGs emptied by 09:20:38, and the load balancer has had no backend to pick, returning 502 failed_to_pick_backend from 09:20:41. The Pods, their /ready probes, the unchanged health check and the firewall are healthy, so a backend health-check or firewall cause is not supported. Why the bundle added tier=frontend is not established.
